correctness.rationale: For each nonzero unit normal u, exact binary support equals 2^(d-2) E|m+X|. Reflection symmetry gives E|m+X| >= E|X|, and Szarek sharp p=1 Khintchine with its equality conditions shows minimum 1/sqrt(2), attained only when u=(e_i-e_j)/sqrt(2). Every such normal annihilates binary generators spanning a (d-1)-hyperplane, hence is a facet. Their positive/equality supports force any optimal inball center onto the diagonal; all other finitely many facet inequalities are strict at zero and permit a nonzero diagonal interval. Coordinate bounds determine the circumradius and exactly two antipodal contacts. Exhaustive normal checks through dimension five and random checks through dimension ten support, but do not replace, the all-dimensional proof. Reference: arXiv:1207.2229v2 Theorem 7 and its proof.

The sharp Khintchine input is known and credited; the specific exact facet recursion and center-dimensionality are new best-knowledge deductions. value.rationale: The White Whale is a canonical high-combinatorial-complexity polytope whose nearest Euclidean support facets simplify to a quadratic family. The finding identifies exactly all contacting facets, proves they recursively realize a lower-dimensional White Whale, and determines the affine dimension and direction of the entire optimal ball-center set (positive despite central symmetry). This is a natural complete facet-contact and center-dimension classification for every dimension, with a precise anisotropy ratio; its relevance is structural and not merely an isolated evaluation of the known Khintchine bound.
